record.title: A paper reports trace-audited human-agent teams conducting synchrotron X-ray experiments
record.summary: An arXiv preprint submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC describes VISION-CC, a team of specialized coding agents grounded in validated scientific tools, conducting three human-guided synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven’s NSLS-II 11-BM beamline. The authors report complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts and an audit pipeline for decision provenance. Their audit estimates that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while methodological/scientific contributions rose from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. The authors describe the interaction shares as approximate and limit the study to one scientist, beamline and agent platform. The team, audit codebook, a subset of experimental frames and a sanitized ledger excerpt are available; full audit data are available by request. In a supplemental verified-link analysis, authors also report that human-proposed ideas reached code edits in 48–61% of cases, versus 36–45% for the team lead and 25–30% for the agent cogs; those are author-coded links, not independent measurements of impact.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record lists v1 of the preprint on auditable human-agent teams for autonomous X-ray experimentation as submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that VISION-CC conducted three human-guided transmission small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven National Laboratory’s NSLS-II 11-BM CMS beamline, using specialized agent roles and validated scientific software for instrument operation, analysis and adaptive sampling.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, and that methodological/scientific contributions rose from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. Supplemental Table S12 reports low agreement between external human raters and the pipeline for broad message/coordination labels (Cohen’s κ about 0.11–0.48 across sampled categories), despite stronger agreement between the pipeline’s own raters; the headline synthesis share therefore remains approximate.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper and linked author repository expose the VISION-CC agent/configuration files and audit codebook/prompts, 44 losslessly compressed SAXS frames from Exp2, and a sanitized 25-minute Exp2 audit-ledger excerpt. The repository says more code will follow; the paper says full audit data are available by reasonable request subject to facility security policy.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed paper does not establish that the workflow or audit findings generalize beyond one scientist, one beamline and one agent platform, or that the reported results have been independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a verified-link analysis across three experiments, the authors report that human-proposed ideas reached code edits in 48–61% of cases, compared with 36–45% for the Team Lead and 25–30% for the agent cogs. The linked finding rates were 24–38%, 23–27%, and 16–23%, respectively. These are author-reported pipeline links, not independent or causal estimates of contribution.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group has reproduced the workflow, experiment outcomes or audit statistics in the reviewed evidence.
Evidence comes from one scientist, one beamline and one agent platform; transfer across facilities, teams, tasks or models is unknown.

The authors report low agreement between external human raters and the pipeline for broad message/coordination labels (Cohen’s κ about 0.11–0.48 across sampled categories); agreement between the pipeline’s own raters is higher. The 61–67% synthesis share is therefore approximate, and full transcripts/audit data are not openly available.
No matched measurement of experiment quality, cycle time, engineering labor or total cost against a non-agent workflow was identified.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported workflow and trace-based audit transfer, they could change how physical-science agents are engineered and evaluated; the evidence is a single-scientist, one-beamline case and does not establish generality.
limitations: Single-scientist, one-beamline, one-platform case series; no demonstrated cross-domain generality.

Broad message/coordination classifications have low external inter-rater agreement (reported Cohen’s κ about 0.11–0.48 across sampled categories); pipeline-internal raters agree more strongly. The headline synthesis share is approximate.
No independent reproduction or matched baseline for scientific outcome, cycle time, labor or cost.
Full audit data are request-only; the public release contains selected data and a sanitized ledger excerpt.
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint submitted on 6 November 2026 at 08:33:55 UTC describes VISION-CC, a team of specialized coding agents grounded in validated scientific tools, conducting three human-guided synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering experiments on nanoparticle superlattices at Brookhaven’s NSLS-II 11-BM beamline. The authors report complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts and an audit pipeline for decision provenance. Their audit estimates that 61–67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while methodological/scientific contributions rose from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56–61% in later experiments. The authors describe the interaction shares as approximate and limit the study to one scientist, beamline and agent platform. The team, audit codebook, a subset of experimental frames and a sanitized ledger excerpt are available; full audit data are available by request. In a supplemental verified-link analysis, authors also report that human-proposed ideas reached code edits in 48–61% of cases, versus 36–45% for the team lead and 25–30% for the agent cogs; those are author-coded links, not independent measurements of impact.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report sustained natural-language-guided physical experiments and aggregate audit statistics for three experiment sessions; these are paper-reported findings, not independently reproduced results.
technical.compute_or_cost: No comparable end-to-end model/API expenditure or cost-per-experiment baseline was identified in the reviewed sections.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint and linked availability statement establish that the authors report these experiments, audit procedures and partial artifacts. The actual experimental runs and audit classifications were not independently verified in this activation.
technical.mechanism: VISION-CC uses Claude Code agent teams with specialized Operator, Analyst, Gaussian-process and reporting roles grounded by domain-specific instructions and validated tools (Bluesky beamline control, SciAnalysis X-ray analysis and gpCAM adaptive sampling). An Audit cog reconstructs proposals, decisions and corrections from retained human-agent and agent-agent transcripts.
technical.regime: Three transmission small-angle X-ray scattering sessions on two nanoparticle-superlattice samples at NSLS-II 11-BM CMS, guided by one scientist and implemented with one agent platform.
technical.reproducibility: The linked author repository contains VISION-CC team/configuration files and the audit codebook/prompts, 44 losslessly compressed Exp2 SAXS frames, and one sanitized 25-minute Exp2 audit-ledger excerpt; its README says more code will follow. The paper says full audit data are available by reasonable request subject to facility security policy. No code execution or independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The study is a descriptive case series; it does not provide a matched non-agent baseline for experiment quality, time, cost or scientific discovery.

brief.title: A paper reports trace-audited human-agent teams conducting synchrotron X-ray experiments
brief.why_it_matters: If trace-audited agent teams can lower the engineering barrier to physical experimentation, they could extend agentic systems from computational workflows into real scientific instruments. This paper offers a concrete but narrow case and a decision-provenance approach; it does not show general scientific autonomy, independent replication or improved experiment economics.
